title: 2026-11-05_KAITEN_Botnet_Investigation_bbb
description: Investigate a compromised host to identify and mitigate the KAITEN botnet activity.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The KAITEN botnet is a Linux-based malware family that spreads through Telnet scanning and establishes command-and-control (C2) connections. It performs network scanning and can be used for various malicious activities, including distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. In this scenario, you will investigate a compromised host to identify and mitigate the KAITEN botnet activity.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can use standard Linux commands and tools to investigate the system. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can use standard Linux commands and tools to investigate the system. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify the Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. List all services: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.
2. Filter running services: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to filter only the running services.
3. Inspect suspicious services: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that might be related to network communication.
4. Identify the beacon service: The service responsible for sending beacon to the C2 server is likely to have a name or description indicating network activity or health monitoring.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Filter the list to show only running services with `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that might indicate network activity.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the beacon service: Use the command `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service` to view the service configuration.
2. Identify the ExecStart command: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
3. Examine the beacon script: Use a text editor or `cat` command to view the contents of the script specified in the `ExecStart` command.
4. Find the communication port: Search for the port number in the script, which is likely to be specified in a command like `nc` (netcat) or similar network utility.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service` to view the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Examine the script specified in the `ExecStart` command to find the communication port.

levels.title: Identify the Scheduling Component
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.
2. Identify the relevant timer: Look for a timer that is associated with the `bot-beacon.service`.
3. Inspect the timer configuration: Use the command `systemctl cat bot-beacon.timer` to view the timer configuration.
4. Understand the scheduling: The timer configuration will show how often the service is scheduled to run.

hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for a timer associated with the `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat bot-beacon.timer` to view the timer configuration.
